author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader filters the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Both published forms of the vet directory accept an optional specialty and then show only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring case. A blank or absent value lists every veterinarian. Paging keeps the filter. No page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: /vets.html?specialty=<name> shows only vets holding that specialty; /vets?specialty=<name> returns only those vets
matching is on the whole specialty name and is case-insensitive; a prefix or other partial name matches no vet
a vet holding several specialties matches whenever any one of them is the requested specialty
a specialty no vet holds yields the normal page or JSON document with an empty vet list and HTTP 200; it is not distinguished from a specialty that does not exist
an empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if the parameter were absent, listing every vet
a value padded with leading or trailing spaces is not trimmed, so it matches no vet
without the parameter both surfaces behave exactly as they do today, including the JSON list staying unpaged
paging applies to the filtered HTML list, and its pagination links carry the specialty parameter
neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or other on-page control for choosing a specialty
searching or filtering pets and visits
reinstating the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 or reusing its id
notes: Four choices the owner left open were taken on the narrowest reading and recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than consulted, per the intake record (line 2): one requirement covers both surfaces; a padded value is not trimmed; the machine-readable list stays unpaged; the on-page control is a deferred follow-up. Two follow-ups outside my write scope, for the system-design-expert: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-14-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md, and system-design.md's known-defect row calling the machine-readable vet route requirement-less is now stale — it is supported under REQ-VET-003.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice is the owner search-with-paging shape applied to the vet package: a derived repository query, an optional request parameter on the controller, and the value echoed into the model so pagination links carry it. No new package, type, layer, or dependency. Both filtered surfaces read through VetRepository, keeping the filter out of controller code and off the pattern catalog's Web controller row. The genuinely new ground is caching: VetRepository's two existing reads are @Cacheable("vets") and the cache has no size limit or eviction, so the filtered reads must not be annotated. That decision is now ADR 2026-08-14-uncached-filtered-vet-queries.md, with the rule stated in system-design.md, § Persistence. Basis for the covering-symbol claims: VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, OwnerRepository.java, OwnerController.java and CacheConfiguration.java read directly; no IDE oracle is connected in this run, so no symbol-resolution call backs them.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived reads matching the joined specialty name whole and case-insensitively: a Page<Vet> for the HTML surface and a Collection<Vet> for the JSON surface. Neither carries a caching annotation
VetController's two handlers each gain an optional specialty request parameter and select between the filtered and the unfiltered repository read
the HTML handler puts the active specialty on the model so vets/vetList.html pagination links can carry it; no form or control is added to the page
the JSON surface keeps returning the Vets wrapper and stays unpaged
no schema, seed-data, message-bundle, or dependency change: specialties.name and the vet_specialties join table already exist on all three vendors

patterns.description: derived query with Pageable — the precedent for putting a list filter in the repository rather than in the controller
the controller normalizing an absent search value before delegating — the precedent for blank-means-unfiltered, but note it calls strip() and REQ-VET-003 does not (see risks)
the two @Cacheable("vets") reads the new methods sit beside; the new ones are deliberately unannotated per ADR 2026-08-14-uncached-filtered-vet-queries.md

risks.risk: specialties.name is a plain VARCHAR on H2 and TEXT on PostgreSQL, so a derived equality match is case-sensitive on every vendor. Relying on a column type for case-insensitivity is how the PostgreSQL owner-search defect happened (system-design.md, Known Defects)
risks.mitigation: put case-insensitivity in the query with Spring Data's IgnoreCase keyword, not in the schema. The H2-backed suite then catches a regression, which it cannot do for the owner-search defect

risks.risk: annotating the filtered reads @Cacheable("vets") for symmetry with their siblings would let an unauthenticated caller add an entry per distinct specialty string to a cache with no size limit and no eviction
risks.mitigation: decided against and recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-14-uncached-filtered-vet-queries.md; the rule is stated in system-design.md, § Persistence. A reviewer reading the asymmetry as an oversight should be pointed at that ADR

risks.risk: vets/vetList.html builds every pagination href by string preprocessing (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}). Interpolating a request-supplied specialty the same way writes an unencoded reflected value into an href
risks.mitigation: use the link-expression parameter form, @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes each value. This is the security-principles cross-site-scripting row applied to an attribute context

risks.risk: when no filter is active, a null model value rendered through a link expression can emit a trailing empty specialty= on every pagination link, contradicting the criterion that the unfiltered surface behaves exactly as today
risks.mitigation: theAbsentSpecialtyShouldLeaveBothSurfacesUnchanged pins the unfiltered markup; keep the parameter out of the link when no filter is active rather than passing an empty value

risks.risk: REQ-VET-003 does not trim a padded value, while the owner search at OwnerController:103 calls strip(). Copying the owner precedent wholesale would silently violate the padded-value criterion
risks.mitigation: normalize only blank-to-absent (a hasText check) and pass the value through untouched otherwise. Recorded as an open question below, since the owner precedent argues the other way

risks.risk: a Pageable over a query that joins an EAGER collection can make Hibernate apply the limit in memory (HHH000104)
risks.mitigation: the specialties join is a filter join, not a fetch join, so this should not fire; theFilteredVetPageShouldCarryTheSpecialtyOnItsPaginationLinks and the filtered-list test should assert total count and page contents, not just presence

notes: Both documentation follow-ups the product expert flagged in the prd-entry are judged valid and applied. (1) docs/adr/README.md was missing an index row for 2026-08-14-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md; the row is added, together with one for the new caching ADR. (2) The system-design.md Known Defects row calling the machine-readable vet route requirement-less was stale the moment REQ-VET-003 landed in the PRD; the row is removed. The route's Contracts-table Implements wiring is deliberately NOT updated here: that column asserts the code satisfies the requirement, which will only be true once the filter ships, so it belongs to doc-sync after implementation. One further system-design.md change came out of this triage: Open Question 5 now records that the paged read's cache key already carries an unbounded caller-supplied page number, which the new ADR's Context depends on. || Open questions recorded rather than consulted, per the intake at line 2 (no further product answer is available): (a) the padded-value rule diverges from the owner search, which strips — a later owner may want them consistent; (b) whether the JSON surface should ever be paged, deferred with the requirement leaving it unpaged; (c) whether a specialty name no vet holds should ever be distinguishable from one that does not exist, which the empty-list-with-200 answer forecloses for now; (d) if the on-page control follow-up arrives, the parameter contract fixed here is what it must bind to. || The H2 vet_specialties table has no unique constraint on (vet_id, specialty_id) while PostgreSQL does; a duplicate pairing would duplicate a vet in the joined result. Seed data has none, so no Distinct is needed today. || No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge.

author: code-quality-reviewer
recommendations: VetController.java:86 — the private activeSpecialty() javadoc cites 'REQ-VET-003' directly ('REQ-VET-003 does not trim it...'). No other production file in the codebase references a requirement ID in a code comment; the ID is only meaningful by cross-referencing docs/prd.md, and requirement IDs can be renumbered or archived. Rephrasing the sentence to describe the behavior directly (drop the ID) would keep the comment self-contained for a reader with no access to today's PRD.

vetList.html — the pagination block repeats the same 'specialty != null ? @{...(...,specialty=...)} : @{...(...)}' ternary five times (lines ~339-372). Thymeleaf's link-expression syntax makes a shared helper awkward, so this is not a blocking finding, but a th:with-scoped variable or a Thymeleaf fragment parameter could collapse the five near-identical branches if the template gains a sixth link.
approved_aspects: VetController's activeSpecialty() blank-to-null normalization mirrors OwnerController's established lastName pattern (null-check plus a documented sentinel), keeping the new surface consistent with the codebase's existing convention rather than introducing Optional where the rest of the package does not use it

VetRepository's two new derived-query methods are documented with why they are deliberately not @Cacheable, with a direct pointer to the ADR, so the asymmetry with the sibling cached methods reads as a decision rather than an oversight
Formatting (./gradlew checkFormat) passes clean; naming, method length, and control flow throughout VetController and VetRepository meet the checklist

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain check NOT RUN, not clean: build.gradle configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin (plugins are boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm 1.1.2, cyclonedx-bom 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47), and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran. This change adds no dependency and does not alter build.gradle, so the delta introduces no supply-chain risk; the resolved framework versions (Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Jackson) remain unverified against the NVD by CI or a human. The project already emits a CycloneDX SBOM, which is the natural feed for that check.

Readability-adjacent, no exploit path: vetList.html line 20 declares a th:each local named 'specialty' (a Specialty entity) while the model attribute 'specialty' (a String) drives the pagination links. The scopes do not overlap today — the loop is confined to the table body — so rendering is correct, but a future edit that moves a link inside the table would silently read the wrong 'specialty'. Renaming the loop variable would remove the trap.

Request-supplied specialty length is unbounded (only the container's query-string limit applies) before it reaches the database comparison. Harmless at this scale and no worse than the existing unfiltered reads; worth a length cap if the filter ever gains a cached or indexed path.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: both new reads are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) with the request value bound as a JPA parameter. No concatenated query text, no @Query, no createQuery anywhere in the vet package.

Cross-site scripting on the reflected filter: the model attribute 'specialty' is request-derived and reaches the page only through link expressions @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encode the value; Thymeleaf's default attribute escaping stays on. The change also removes the last __${...}__ preprocessing hrefs from vetList.html, so the file no longer builds any URL by string interpolation. thePaginationLinksShouldUrlEncodeTheSpecialty pins the encoding with a <script> payload (specialty=%3Cscript%3E), and grep over src/main/resources/templates finds no th:utext, no param.* access, and no remaining preprocessing.

Cache abuse avoided: the two new reads carry no @Cacheable, so request-supplied text never becomes a key in the unbounded, evictionless 'vets' cache. Deliberate per docs/adr/2026-08-14-uncached-filtered-vet-queries.md, restated in the Javadoc on both methods; the asymmetry with the sibling findAll reads is the secure choice, not an oversight.

Exposed surface unchanged: no new route. Both handlers gain one optional @RequestParam String; no request-bound command object, so no mass-assignment or identifier-binding surface. Blank-to-absent normalization (StringUtils.hasText) happens at the controller boundary, matching the owner-search precedent.

Transaction and pattern consistency: both new methods carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) like every existing VetRepository read — least privilege on the data access, and the same way the neighbouring concern is already secured.

No secrets, no logging, no file or process I/O, no deserialization config, no schema or dependency change in the diff: grep over the change set for password/secret/token/api-key/credential returns nothing, and no System.out/err, Runtime, or ProcessBuilder appears in the vet package.

Resource exposure not worsened: the paged filter joins the specialties association as a filter join rather than a fetch join, so paging stays in SQL; the unpaged JSON surface returns a filtered subset of what /vets already returned unfiltered.
